comp-limbs-001.subject: anatomy
comp-limbs-001.prompt: After an acromioclavicular injury, the trapezoid and acromioclavicular ligaments are torn but the conoid remains intact. Which residual mechanical behavior is most consistent with this pattern?
comp-limbs-001.learningObjective: Predict residual acromioclavicular mechanics after selective conoid, trapezoid and capsular injuries.

comp-limbs-002.subject: anatomy
comp-limbs-002.prompt: Stress testing shows excessive anteroposterior translation at the acromioclavicular joint but near-normal vertical suspension of the scapula. Which injury best fits?
comp-limbs-002.learningObjective: Distinguish horizontal acromioclavicular instability from failure of vertical coracoclavicular suspension.

comp-limbs-003.subject: anatomy
comp-limbs-003.prompt: An intra-articular fibrocartilaginous structure is detached from the posterosuperior medial clavicle and from the first costal cartilage near the sternum. Which joint function is most directly compromised?
comp-limbs-003.learningObjective: Relate sternoclavicular disc attachments to joint partition and stability.

comp-limbs-004.subject: anatomy
comp-limbs-004.prompt: Imaging shows a capsular defect between the superior edge of subscapularis and anterior edge of supraspinatus. Which pair normally reinforces this interval?
comp-limbs-004.learningObjective: Localize the rotator interval and its ligamentous reinforcements.

comp-limbs-005.subject: anatomy
comp-limbs-005.prompt: During a shoulder arthrogram, contrast exits through the normal anterior capsular opening below the coracoid and surrounds the upper border of subscapularis. Which interpretation best fits the anatomy?
comp-limbs-005.learningObjective: Distinguish normal subscapular bursal filling from an abnormal capsular leak.

comp-limbs-006.subject: anatomy
comp-limbs-006.prompt: External rotation is weak and infraspinatus is denervated, but supraspinatus contraction is preserved. Which location best explains an isolated suprascapular neuropathy with this pattern?
comp-limbs-006.learningObjective: Localize suprascapular injury using discordant supraspinatus and infraspinatus findings.

comp-limbs-007.subject: anatomy
comp-limbs-007.prompt: After a focal posterior-wall axillary injury, teres major and the lower part of subscapularis are weak, while latissimus dorsi and deltoid are preserved. Which branch is most likely interrupted?
comp-limbs-007.learningObjective: Distinguish lower subscapular injury from neighboring posterior-cord branch injuries.

comp-limbs-008.subject: anatomy
comp-limbs-008.prompt: A branch crossing anterior to the axillary vessels is divided where it pierces clavipectoral fascia. Pectoralis major loses part of its innervation, but musculocutaneous motor function remains normal. Which localization is best?
comp-limbs-008.learningObjective: Use fascial course and spared lateral-cord functions to localize a lateral pectoral lesion.

comp-limbs-009.subject: anatomy
comp-limbs-009.prompt: A lesion confined to the anterior branch of the axillary nerve weakens the anterior deltoid. Which preserved finding would best support that localization rather than injury of the entire axillary trunk?
comp-limbs-009.learningObjective: Distinguish anterior axillary-branch injury from injury of the whole axillary nerve.

comp-limbs-010.subject: anatomy
comp-limbs-010.prompt: A small penetrating wound lateral to the biceps tendon causes anterolateral forearm numbness. Biceps and brachialis retain normal power. Which structure is most consistent with the lesion?
comp-limbs-010.learningObjective: Separate distal musculocutaneous sensory injury from proximal motor involvement.

comp-limbs-011.subject: anatomy
comp-limbs-011.prompt: A radial-head fracture is accompanied by distal radioulnar instability. Under axial load the radius migrates proximally. Which additional lesion best unifies the findings?
comp-limbs-011.learningObjective: Integrate radial-head injury, distal instability and longitudinal forearm load transfer.

comp-limbs-012.subject: anatomy
comp-limbs-012.prompt: Following loss of the radial head, the elbow remains stable under valgus stress until one ligament complex is also disrupted. Which structure is the principal remaining restraint?
comp-limbs-012.learningObjective: Predict valgus instability after combined radial-head and medial ligament failure.

comp-limbs-013.subject: anatomy
comp-limbs-013.prompt: Two equal-sized tears involve the triangular fibrocartilage: one is central and one peripheral. Why does the central lesion have less intrinsic vascular support for repair?
comp-limbs-013.learningObjective: Relate triangular fibrocartilage tear position to its intrinsic vascular repair potential.

comp-limbs-014.subject: anatomy
comp-limbs-014.prompt: With the ulna approximately fixed, imaging tracks pronation. Which paired movement is expected?
comp-limbs-014.learningObjective: Integrate proximal and distal radioulnar movements during pronation.

comp-limbs-015.subject: anatomy
comp-limbs-015.prompt: A patient has weak rapid, resisted supination with the elbow flexed, but can still perform slow unresisted supination with the elbow extended. Which muscle's loss best explains the disproportionate deficit?
comp-limbs-015.learningObjective: Use load and elbow position to distinguish contributions to supination.

comp-limbs-016.subject: anatomy
comp-limbs-016.prompt: Contrast in the inferior ulnar collateral artery crosses to the ulnar arterial system anterior to the medial epicondyle. Which returning branch completes this direct anastomosis?
comp-limbs-016.learningObjective: Trace an anterior medial-epicondylar arterial collateral route.

comp-limbs-017.subject: anatomy
comp-limbs-017.prompt: A vessel leaves the common interosseous artery, passes between the oblique cord and proximal border of the interosseous membrane, then descends with the deep radial branch. Which vessel and compartment are involved?
comp-limbs-017.learningObjective: Follow the posterior interosseous artery through the proximal membrane interval.

comp-limbs-018.subject: anatomy
comp-limbs-018.prompt: The median nerve crosses superficial to the ulnar artery in the proximal forearm. What usually lies between these two structures at their crossing?
comp-limbs-018.learningObjective: Identify the muscular partition between median nerve and ulnar artery.

comp-limbs-019.subject: anatomy
comp-limbs-019.prompt: After compression at the distal border of supinator, finger extension fails but wrist extension persists with radial deviation. Cutaneous sensation is normal. Which explanation best fits?
comp-limbs-019.learningObjective: Explain preserved radially deviated wrist extension in a distal deep-radial lesion.

comp-limbs-020.subject: anatomy
comp-limbs-020.prompt: After an operation near the cubital tunnel, finger abduction and ulnar digital sensation remain normal, but a patch of medial forearm skin is numb. Which injury best explains this selective new deficit?
comp-limbs-020.learningObjective: Distinguish medial forearm cutaneous injury from ulnar nerve injury.

comp-limbs-021.subject: anatomy
comp-limbs-021.prompt: Following forced flexion of an extended fingertip, active DIP extension is lost but passive extension is full. Months later the PIP joint hyperextends. What sequence best explains the progression?
comp-limbs-021.learningObjective: Explain secondary PIP hyperextension following terminal extensor disruption.

comp-limbs-022.subject: anatomy
comp-limbs-022.prompt: After a dorsal PIP laceration, a finger initially extends weakly. Later the PIP rests flexed while the DIP hyperextends. Which change converts the lateral extensor bands into PIP flexors?
comp-limbs-022.learningObjective: Relate central-slip failure to lateral-band migration and boutonniere posture.

comp-limbs-023.subject: anatomy
comp-limbs-023.prompt: After forced radial deviation of the thumb MCP joint, its torn ulnar collateral ligament lies superficial to the adductor aponeurosis. Why is direct ligament healing impeded?
comp-limbs-023.learningObjective: Explain impaired healing when adductor aponeurosis intervenes in a thumb UCL tear.

comp-limbs-024.subject: anatomy
comp-limbs-024.prompt: During reconstruction of a finger flexor sheath, which pair of pulleys is most important to retain to limit bowstringing along the proximal and middle phalanges?
comp-limbs-024.learningObjective: Identify the critical digital annular pulleys for preventing bowstringing.

comp-limbs-025.subject: anatomy
comp-limbs-025.prompt: An intact finger allows lateral movement at the MCP joint in extension but very little when that joint is fully flexed. The PIP remains stable in both positions. Which explanation best fits?
comp-limbs-025.learningObjective: Compare position-dependent MCP collateral tension with PIP collateral behavior.

comp-limbs-026.subject: anatomy
comp-limbs-026.prompt: A small deep palmar lesion causes interosseous and adductor-pollicis weakness, but hypothenar muscle function, palmaris brevis and ulnar digital sensation remain intact. Which site best fits?
comp-limbs-026.learningObjective: Localize a deep ulnar lesion by combining spared hypothenar and sensory findings.

comp-limbs-027.subject: anatomy
comp-limbs-027.prompt: A proper palmar digital nerve on the radial side of the index finger is divided near the proximal phalanx. In addition to its palmar field, which sensory area can be lost despite an intact superficial radial nerve?
comp-limbs-027.learningObjective: Predict dorsal distal-digit sensory loss after proper palmar digital nerve injury.

comp-limbs-028.subject: anatomy
comp-limbs-028.prompt: An infection begins within the little-finger flexor synovial sheath. Which proximal route is anatomically most likely in the usual arrangement?
comp-limbs-028.learningObjective: Trace likely spread from the little-finger flexor synovial sheath.

comp-limbs-029.subject: anatomy
comp-limbs-029.prompt: A digital flexor tendon is intact, but thin synovial folds connecting its deep surface near its insertion are cut. Which function has been directly impaired?
comp-limbs-029.learningObjective: Relate the vincula to digital flexor tendon vascular support.

comp-limbs-030.subject: anatomy
comp-limbs-030.prompt: During a palmar dissection, the digital flexor tendons and lumbricals are lifted. An arterial arch lies against the metacarpal bases and interossei with the deep ulnar nerve in its concavity. Which structure is exposed?
comp-limbs-030.learningObjective: Identify the deep palmar arch by tissue plane and associated nerve.

comp-limbs-031.subject: anatomy
comp-limbs-031.prompt: A surgeon exposes the posterior femoral neck near the intertrochanteric crest. Which comparison with the anterior attachment of the hip capsule is correct?
comp-limbs-031.learningObjective: Compare anterior and posterior femoral attachments of the hip capsule.

comp-limbs-032.subject: anatomy
comp-limbs-032.prompt: A painful hip with an effusion is held partly flexed and abducted. Which mechanical explanation best accounts for this posture?
comp-limbs-032.learningObjective: Explain the posture that reduces pressure in an effused hip joint.

comp-limbs-033.subject: anatomy
comp-limbs-033.prompt: A specimen shows thick hyaline cartilage on the anterosuperior acetabular ring, but fat and synovium in its central depression. Which functional interpretation is correct?
comp-limbs-033.learningObjective: Distinguish acetabular load-bearing cartilage from its nonarticular central fossa.

comp-limbs-034.subject: anatomy
comp-limbs-034.prompt: Hip-joint fluid tracks anteriorly into a subtendinous space behind iliopsoas through an aperture between the pubofemoral ligament and descending iliofemoral fibers. Which space is involved?
comp-limbs-034.learningObjective: Trace anterior hip-joint communication with the iliopectineal bursa.

comp-limbs-035.subject: anatomy
comp-limbs-035.prompt: In an adolescent, injury crosses the capital femoral growth plate. Why can the head's circulation be endangered even when vessels within the neck remain patent below the growth plate?
comp-limbs-035.learningObjective: Relate the avascular femoral physis to the route and vulnerability of head vessels.

comp-limbs-036.subject: anatomy
comp-limbs-036.prompt: Two transverse images are obtained: one at the base of the femoral triangle and one at the distal adductor canal. Where is the femoral vein expected relative to its artery at these two levels?
comp-limbs-036.learningObjective: Compare femoral artery-vein relations at two levels of the thigh.

comp-limbs-037.subject: anatomy
comp-limbs-037.prompt: A slowly developing femoral-artery occlusion lies proximal to the profunda femoris origin. Which pathway can deliver collateral blood from the internal iliac system into the thigh beyond the occlusion?
comp-limbs-037.learningObjective: Trace an internal-iliac collateral route beyond proximal femoral occlusion.

comp-limbs-038.subject: anatomy
comp-limbs-038.prompt: A posterior thigh exposure identifies arteries passing through tendinous arches in adductor magnus near the linea aspera. Which arrangement explains their ability to distribute blood longitudinally?
comp-limbs-038.learningObjective: Explain the longitudinal anastomotic network of profunda perforating arteries.

comp-limbs-039.subject: anatomy
comp-limbs-039.prompt: A small vessel leaves the distal adductor canal through its roof with the saphenous nerve and then passes between sartorius and gracilis. Which branch is expected?
comp-limbs-039.learningObjective: Follow the saphenous branch of the descending genicular artery out of the canal.

comp-limbs-040.subject: anatomy
comp-limbs-040.prompt: Following harvesting of the great saphenous vein in the leg, a patient develops medial leg numbness but normal quadriceps strength and foot movements. Which explanation best fits?
comp-limbs-040.learningObjective: Explain a cutaneous deficit after great saphenous vein harvest.

comp-limbs-041.subject: anatomy
comp-limbs-041.prompt: A large knee effusion extends superiorly deep to quadriceps. During knee extension, which small muscle normally pulls the wall of this communicating recess away from the moving joint?
comp-limbs-041.learningObjective: Relate articularis genus to retraction of the suprapatellar synovial recess.

comp-limbs-042.subject: anatomy
comp-limbs-042.prompt: An adult with chronic knee synovitis develops a fluid-filled swelling posteromedially. Imaging places its neck between the semimembranosus tendon and the medial head of gastrocnemius. Which space has distended?
comp-limbs-042.learningObjective: Distinguish the typical Baker-cyst bursa from other knee bursae and recesses.

comp-limbs-043.subject: anatomy
comp-limbs-043.prompt: A reconstruction is being assessed separately in knee flexion and extension. The anterolateral bundle of the posterior cruciate ligament has failed, while the posteromedial bundle is intact. Which mechanical deficit is most directly expected?
comp-limbs-043.learningObjective: Predict position-specific posterior instability from selective PCL bundle failure.

comp-limbs-044.subject: anatomy
comp-limbs-044.prompt: A person can stand with relatively little quadriceps activity when the knees are extended but fatigues rapidly while holding a shallow squat. Which change best explains the increased demand?
comp-limbs-044.learningObjective: Explain why a flexed weight-bearing knee requires sustained quadriceps activity.

comp-limbs-045.subject: anatomy
comp-limbs-045.prompt: Recurrent lateral patellar displacement occurs in a knee with a shallow lateral trochlear wall. Loss of which additional restraint would most compound the deficient bony guidance?
comp-limbs-045.learningObjective: Integrate trochlear geometry and medial soft-tissue restraints in patellar tracking.

comp-limbs-046.subject: anatomy
comp-limbs-046.prompt: After compression at the fibular neck, a patient has weak ankle dorsiflexion and eversion. Inversion against resistance remains strong when tested with the ankle slightly plantarflexed. Why does this pattern favor a common fibular neuropathy over an L5 root lesion?
comp-limbs-046.learningObjective: Use tibialis posterior function to distinguish common fibular from broader L5 injury.

comp-limbs-047.subject: anatomy
comp-limbs-047.prompt: Electrodiagnostic findings show denervation of tibialis anterior, fibularis longus and the short head of biceps femoris. The long head of biceps femoris and tibialis posterior are preserved. Which localization best integrates these findings?
comp-limbs-047.learningObjective: Use short-head biceps involvement to localize a common-fibular-division lesion proximally.

comp-limbs-048.subject: anatomy
comp-limbs-048.prompt: A tight strap at the anterior ankle is followed by first-web-space numbness and weakness of extensor digitorum brevis. Ankle dorsiflexion and long-toe extension are normal. Which explanation best fits?
comp-limbs-048.learningObjective: Distinguish distal deep fibular injury from proximal anterior-compartment denervation.

comp-limbs-049.subject: anatomy
comp-limbs-049.prompt: A small laceration where the superficial fibular nerve pierces the distal leg fascia causes dorsal-foot sensory loss, sparing the first web space. Eversion remains normal. Why can the motor examination be preserved?
comp-limbs-049.learningObjective: Explain preserved eversion after injury of superficial fibular cutaneous branches.

comp-limbs-050.subject: anatomy
comp-limbs-050.prompt: A patient referred for presumed tarsal-tunnel compression has plantar sensory loss, but also clear weakness of tibialis posterior and flexor hallucis longus. Which finding challenges a lesion confined behind the medial malleolus?
comp-limbs-050.learningObjective: Identify proximal tibial motor findings inconsistent with an isolated tarsal-tunnel lesion.

comp-limbs-051.subject: anatomy
comp-limbs-051.prompt: A healed distal tibiofibular fusion leaves normal talocrural cartilage but restricts end-range dorsiflexion. Which normal geometric accommodation has been lost?
comp-limbs-051.learningObjective: Relate talar trochlear geometry to small distal tibiofibular movements.

comp-limbs-052.subject: anatomy
comp-limbs-052.prompt: After an ankle injury, dynamic ultrasound shows fibularis longus and brevis tendons snapping anteriorly over the lateral malleolus. Anterior talar translation is normal. Which injury most directly explains the observed movement?
comp-limbs-052.learningObjective: Distinguish fibular tendon-retinacular failure from talocrural ligament instability.

comp-limbs-053.subject: anatomy
comp-limbs-053.prompt: During a posterior ankle dissection, the flexor hallucis longus muscle-tendon unit is identified. A working interval is maintained on its lateral side. Which important relationship makes that interval protective?
comp-limbs-053.learningObjective: Use flexor hallucis longus to locate the medial posterior-ankle neurovascular bundle.

comp-limbs-054.subject: anatomy
comp-limbs-054.prompt: A small ossicle plantar to the cuboid is displaced after injury, and imaging shows loss of continuity of the tendon that turns medially across the sole toward the first ray. Which tendon should be assessed?
comp-limbs-054.learningObjective: Relate an os peroneum injury to the fibularis longus tendon course.

comp-limbs-055.subject: anatomy
comp-limbs-055.prompt: At the anterior ankle a needle is placed immediately lateral to the extensor hallucis longus tendon. Arterial pulsation is encountered, and a neighboring nerve lies lateral to that artery. Which artery-nerve pair fits this arrangement?
comp-limbs-055.learningObjective: Use extensor hallucis longus to identify the anterior-ankle artery and nerve.

comp-limbs-056.subject: anatomy
comp-limbs-056.prompt: While the foot remains weight-bearing, an examiner passively extends the great toe. The medial longitudinal arch rises even without voluntary intrinsic-muscle contraction. Which mechanism best explains this?
comp-limbs-056.learningObjective: Explain passive arch elevation produced by great-toe extension.

comp-limbs-057.subject: anatomy
comp-limbs-057.prompt: Flexor digitorum longus approaches the lateral toes obliquely from the medial side. Following selective loss of quadratus plantae, its tendons still contract but their pull is less well aligned with the toes. What normal contribution has been removed?
comp-limbs-057.learningObjective: Relate quadratus plantae to correction of the long toe flexor's oblique line of pull.

comp-limbs-058.subject: anatomy
comp-limbs-058.prompt: After a focal medial plantar nerve injury, abductor hallucis, flexor digitorum brevis and the first lumbrical are weak. Which additional weakness belongs to the same motor territory rather than implying lateral plantar involvement?
comp-limbs-058.learningObjective: Distinguish medial from lateral plantar intrinsic motor territories.

comp-limbs-059.subject: anatomy
comp-limbs-059.prompt: A plantar dissection has lifted the flexor tendons and the oblique head of adductor hallucis. An arterial arch is found across the metatarsal bases on the interossei. Which connection completes this arch medially?

comp-limbs-060.subject: anatomy
